sections.heading: Interstate driving, rural roads and trip planning
sections.markdown:
# Interstate driving, rural roads and trip planning

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Plan interstate entrances and exits before departure because interchanges may be far apart. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Before remote highway travel, check fuel, vehicle fluids, tires and the spare. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Watch for merging vehicles and changing traffic flow while monitoring ahead, behind and both sides. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Keep following room and know where a clear escape path is available. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
When entering an interstate, signal and identify enough space to merge safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Begin checking main-road traffic while still on the entrance ramp. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Adjust entrance speed toward the traffic speed while finding a safe gap. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
Existing interstate traffic has priority over a merging vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
Do not assume another driver will see the merging vehicle or move aside for it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
Avoid stopping before merging unless stopping is necessary. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
Weather or road conditions can require driving more slowly than the posted minimum. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A02
Do not squeeze into a traffic gap too small for a safe merge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A02
Before changing lanes for a merge, use mirrors, signal and briefly look to the side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
Avoid unnecessary interstate lane changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
The guide generally directs using the right lane except for passing, a left exit or making room for entering traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
On an interstate with at least three same-direction lanes, the guide describes the middle lane for travel and far-left lane for passing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
A merge sign warns of entering traffic and a possible need to adjust speed or safely change lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Watch near exits for drivers who brake suddenly or move toward the ramp at the last moment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
A space cushion includes room ahead, behind and on each side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
Avoid remaining alongside another vehicle on a multilane road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
Maintain space ahead even if a vehicle behind is following too closely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A03
The guide identifies speed control, lane position and communication as the three tools of space management. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A03
Before an exit, read signs early and move into the required lane one lane at a time. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A03
The guide recommends checking the exit lane position about a mile before the interchange. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Signal in advance when preparing to leave the interstate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
If an exit is missed, continue to another exit instead of stopping or backing on the interstate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
When an exit has a deceleration lane, move completely into it before reducing to the ramp’s posted speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
After leaving the interstate, be alert for a change to two-way traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A04
Rural roads require attention even when traffic is light. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A04
On gravel or dirt, reduce speed and allow more following room because traction is reduced. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A04
Rough, rippled or potholed rural surfaces can affect steering and control. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A04
In road dust, slow, increase following space and use low beams to improve visibility to others. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A04
Narrow rural roads may have little shoulder and steep ditches; watch for narrow bridges and opposing vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A04
Slow for an open metal bridge deck, hold the wheel firmly and leave more space because traction is reduced. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A04
Trees and tall crops can hide a rural intersection or approaching traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A04
At a rural rail crossing without gates or lights, slow, look both ways and prepare to stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0108]
